newsitem.title: USA: US natgas stocks seen down 67-72 bcf in weekly AGA.
newsitem.headline: US natgas stocks seen down 67-72 bcf in weekly AGA.

text.p: U.S. natural gas storage levels were expected to fall by 67-72 billion cubic feet (bcf) when weekly American Gas Association (AGA) data are released later today, industry sources said Wednesday.
The Reuter poll of industry players showed expectations for a drawdown ranged widely from 60 bcf to 95 bcf for the week ended Dec 13.
"There were some utilities injecting gas into storage last week. I'm not sure how much, but it was definitely happening. It was pretty mild," said one trader.
Last week's draw of 72 bcf left stocks at 214 bcf, or 8.3 percent, below year-ago, which was in line with expectations between 70 and 80 bcf. The four week average drawdown is 82 bcf.
In last report, eastern stocks fell by 40 bcf to 84 percent of capacity but were still slightly above year-ago. Producing and consuming region west stocks continued to significantly lag 1995 levels.

For the same week last year, total inventories dove 178 bcf when severely cold weather made an early arrival to most of the U.S. A draw today in the expected range would narrow the gap to last year to about 106 bcf. In 1995, eastern storage fell by 128 bcf, while producing stocks dropped by 41 bcf and western stocks by nine bcf.
